e.etymology: From Hawaiian na koa, the brave or the warriors; koa is both the word for a warrior and the name of the islands' prized hardwood tree.
A phonetic spelling of Aiden favored by Spanish-speaking families in the United States. Aiden is from Irish Aodhan, a pet form of Aodh, fire.
A recent name among Spanish-speaking families in the United States, with no documented source. It matches dalet, the fourth letter of the Hebrew alphabet, whose name means door.
A 19th-century coinage, probably modeled on similar-sounding names such as Charlene and Arlette. American use was highest in the 1930s.

assoc.t: Arlene, Garfield's pink cat girlfriend

e.etymology: From Old French Melisende, from the Germanic name Amalaswintha, built from words for work and strength. The Normans brought it to England, where it has been used since the Middle Ages.
namesakes: Millicent Simmonds (actress in A Quiet Place)

e.etymology: A Latin American spelling of Estefania, the Spanish form of Stephanie, shaped by the English pronunciation. All go back to Greek stephanos, a crown or wreath.
A spelling of Evelina, the Latinate form of the Norman name Aveline, made fashionable by Fanny Burney's 1778 novel Evelina. The Eva- spelling links it to Eva.
From Arabic zayna, the feminine of zayn, beauty or adornment. It belongs with Zayn, Zaina and Zainab.
From Old English Ceadda, of obscure meaning, the name of a 7th-century Anglo-Saxon bishop and saint. It was revived in the 20th century and peaked in the United States in the 1970s.
namesakes: Chad Michael Murray (One Tree Hill actor)
Chad Johnson (NFL receiver known as Ochocinco)

assoc.t: Chad, internet slang for a cocky alpha male
Chad, country in north-central Africa
hanging chad, from the 2000 Florida recount

e.note: Chad is internet slang for a brash, privileged alpha male, and also the name of an African country.

e.etymology: From Arabic sayf, sword. It is often the first part of compound names such as Saifuddin, sword of the faith, and Saifullah, sword of God.
From Arabic mahir, skilled or proficient, the active participle of mahara, to be skilled. Maher is the same name in another spelling.
A spelling of Sapphira, from Greek Sappheire, from sappheiros, the blue gemstone. Sapphira appears in the Book of Acts, and Saphira is the dragon in Christopher Paolini's Eragon novels.

assoc.t: Saphira, the blue dragon of the Eragon novels

e.note: In the Bible (Acts 5) Sapphira is struck dead for lying, a story churchgoers may recall.

e.etymology: A modern American name from the Kay- family, one of many forms alongside Kaylin, Kaylyn and Kaelyn. For boys it also echoes Kalen and Jaylen.
A surname turned first name, in American use since the late 1800s. Its source is uncertain.
namesakes: Arlen Specter (longtime US senator from Pennsylvania)

assoc.t: Arlen, Texas, fictional town of King of the Hill

e.etymology: Several names share this spelling: Turkish Ela, from the word for hazel eyes; the Polish short form of Elzbieta, Elizabeth; and an Indian name. Some American parents also use it as a trim spelling of Ella.
A modern American name with no documented older source. It follows the sound of Aaliyah and Kalia, and Kaliyah is its most common spelling.
A short form of Valentin and Valentina, from Latin valens, strong and healthy. It is a familiar nickname in Spanish-speaking countries that American parents now give as a full name.
From Japanese koi, the word for carp, which English borrowed for the ornamental pond fish. A different Japanese word koi means romantic love and is used as a girls' name in Japan.

assoc.t: koi, the colorful ornamental pond carp

e.etymology: A 20th-century American coinage, possibly inspired by Sheila. In India a similar name, Shaila, comes from the Sanskrit word for mountain and is a name of the goddess Parvati.
A 20th-century coinage that adds the feminine -a to Jessie, the pet form of Jessica, on the model of Jenna from Jenny.
namesakes: Jessa Duggar Seewald (19 Kids and Counting reality star)

e.etymology: From the English word rebel, from Latin rebellis, one who makes war again. Parents began using it as a first name in the 2000s.
namesakes: Rebel Wilson (Australian star of Pitch Perfect)

assoc.t: rebel, one who resists authority
Rebels, Confederate soldiers; Ole Miss Rebels teams
Canon EOS Rebel cameras
the Rebel Alliance of Star Wars

e.note: Rebel was the nickname for Confederate soldiers, a link that lingers in the American South.

e.etymology: A respelling of Elowen, a modern Cornish name taken from elowen, the Cornish word for elm tree. The spelling brings in Ella and the -wyn ending of Welsh names such as Bronwyn.
An elaboration of Lucia, from Latin lux, light, with the ending -inda. Cervantes used it for a character in Don Quixote (1605), and it later passed from fiction into everyday English use.
The continental European form of Rosemary, a combination of Rose and Marie that honors the Virgin Mary with her flower. It later also recalled the herb rosemary.
namesakes: Rosemarie DeWitt (actress in Rachel Getting Married and Mad Men)

e.etymology: A respelling of Delaney that brings out the nickname Lainey. Delaney is a Norman surname, from Old French del aunaie, from the alder grove, and in Ireland an English form of O Dubhshlaine.
In the United States mostly the Spanish name German, from Latin germanus, brother, the name of several early saints. Russian German is a separate name, the local form of Hermann.

assoc.t: German, the nationality and language

e.note: Written without the Spanish accent, it reads in English as the nationality German; the name is said her-MAHN.

e.etymology: From Sanskrit priya, dear or beloved. It is one of the most common Hindu girls' names and often forms compounds such as Haripriya, beloved of Hari.
Created by J.R.R. Tolkien from Old English eoh, horse, and wynn, joy, for the shieldmaiden of Rohan who kills the Witch-king in The Lord of the Rings.

assoc.t: Eowyn, shieldmaiden in The Lord of the Rings

e.note: Tolkien wrote it with an accent as Éowyn; people who have not read the books may stumble over saying it.

e.etymology: A spelling of Phineas that starts with Finn. Phineas is the English form of the biblical Phinehas, Hebrew Pinchas, a name most scholars trace to Egyptian pa-nehesy, the Nubian.
namesakes: Finneas O'Connell (Grammy-winning producer and Billie Eilish's brother)

assoc.t: Finneas, singer-producer and Billie Eilish's brother
Phineas of Disney's Phineas and Ferb (same sound)

e.etymology: The short form of Steven and Stephen, from Greek stephanos, a crown or wreath. It was given as a full name in its own right from the mid-1900s.
namesakes: Steve Harvey (comedian and Family Feud host)

assoc.t: Steve, the default Minecraft player character
Steve, original host of Blue's Clues
Steve Madden shoes

e.etymology: A contracted form of Katarina, from Greek Aikaterine. The Greek name's source is unknown, but Christians long linked it to katharos, pure.

assoc.t: hurricane that devastated New Orleans in 2005
Katrina and the Waves, Walking on Sunshine band

e.note: Still strongly tied to Hurricane Katrina (2005); American use of the name fell sharply afterward.

e.etymology: From an English surname, Garrett with -son added, so son of Garrett. It matches the English word garrison, the troops stationed in a fort.
namesakes: Garrison Keillor (creator of A Prairie Home Companion)

assoc.t: garrison, the troops stationed at a fort
